We'd like to explore renewal options that make it easier for us to add capacity mid-contract without a heavy administrative lift. Specifically: modular add-on bundles, clearer uplift discount bands, and a simpler co-term path so we can align to our fiscal year.

Attached is a short usage snapshot so you can see the distribution across environments. Can your team share 2–3 practical paths (one conservative, one balanced, one aggressive) and the corresponding price/credit mechanics? Also flag any timing or procurement constraints for invoice/proration.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call next week if useful.

Erin — thanks for the note and the snapshot. I reviewed usage and sketched three pragmatic paths below. I've attached a lightweight workbook so you can see the math with your actual numbers.

Quick summary (high level):
- Modular baseline + burst add-ons: keep base commit, purchase time-bound burst bundles billed at a slightly higher rate but refundable as credits if you convert to committed capacity within 30 days. Good for short spikes.
- Gradual uplift bands: quarterly uplift bands (0–25%, 25–50%, 50%+) with a stepped discount schedule: small upticks get no discount, mid-band gets 5% off uplift tokens, top-band gets 10% off uplift tokens. Commits convert pro-rata to the annualized view at renewal.
- Annualize with smoothing credits: you commit to an annualized forecast but can draw flex credits mid-year that amortize over remaining months; this smooths invoices and keeps unit economics predictable.

Key implementation notes:
- Co-terming: we can offer pro-rated conversion and optional invoice split (base invoice + uplift invoice) to match your procurement cycles.
- Bridge credit: for partial-month growth we typically offer a small bridge credit (1–7% depending on size) to avoid double-billing when customers convert mid-billing cycle.

Proposed next steps:
1) I can run a quick workbook with the numbers you sent and return a single-sheet proposal.
2) If you like one of the paths, we'll loop in Ben (finance ops) for approval on any one-time credits and Lauren for contractual co-term language.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call to finalize mechanics and DocuSign path.

Attaching: modular-pack-workbook.xlsx (worksheet: uplift-scenarios)

Thanks — available Wed/Thu afternoons PT.

—Priyom

Subject: RE: Renewal planning: packaging flexibility for mid-contract growth — pricing check

Looping in finance and ops for a quick read. Priyom's proposed structure looks reasonable from a commercial standpoint; a couple of guardrails we should commit to before we present to Lumenix:

- One-time onboarding/bridge credit: recommend cap at 7% of the incremental uplift invoice for mid-cycle converts (documented as a single-line credit).
- Ongoing uplift discount: recommend standard 5% for 25–50% uplift band, 10% for >50% uplift band (applied to uplift tokens only).
- Invoice mechanics: allow invoice-splitting but require clear PO lines so procurement can accept two invoices per month if they choose.

Ben — can you confirm gross margin impact and whether a one-time 7% credit is within standard approval limits or needs exec sign-off? If it needs exec sign-off, we'll flag it in the deck.

Thanks — I'll draft the co-term clause language once we have the green light on credits.

—Lauren
